themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 4 this week versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—signaling either rapid illegal dispensary expansion or enforcement crackdowns in Mott Haven/Melrose.
evidence: 4 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score 7.49)
Statistically extreme outlier: highest z-score among all tracked complaint categories this cycle
No prior Reddit discussions or news coverage suggests this is newly visible or newly occurring
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed or illegal cannabis retailers opening in the district faster than enforcement can respond? Interview NYPD, DOH, and affected residents.
How many legal cannabis retailers are licensed in CD201 vs. complaints filed? Map the geography of complaints to identify hotspots.

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints surged to 11 this week versus a baseline of 4.8 per week—a 132% increase (z-score: 3.15)—suggesting new bars, restaurants, construction, or nightlife venues operating in the district.
evidence: 11 noise - commercial complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (132% spike, z-score 3.15)
Residential noise also elevated at 1,973 complaints over 90 days, indicating broader quality-of-life concern
No corresponding street sweeping or sidewalk noise issues suggest source is venue-based, not traffic
reporting_angles: Which commercial establishments (bars, restaurants, clubs, construction sites) are newly operating or recently opened in Mott Haven? Are they licensed and soundproofed per code?
Interview residents on 311 complaint addresses to identify which specific blocks are affected and whether complaints led to enforcement.

themes_detail.label: Homeless Services Request Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 12 last week versus a baseline of 2.4 per week—a 405% increase (z-score: 3.52)—indicating either a visible encampment spike or heightened community reporting of unhoused individuals.
evidence: 12 homeless person assistance complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (405% spike, z-score 3.52)
Community board budget requests repeatedly cite 'other requests for services for the homeless' (Department of Homeless Services), indicating a long-standing, unsolved problem now accelerating
No constituent services or CB meeting data available to triangulate whether this is visible street encampment or welfare calls
reporting_angles: Are there visible encampments on specific blocks in Mott Haven or Melrose? Interview DHS, NYPD Outreach, and local residents on where the spike is concentrated.
How many shelter beds exist in or near CD201, and what is current capacity/utilization? Is the spike tied to shelter closures or seasonal migration?

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints spiked to 6 this week versus a baseline of 1.2 per week—a 380% increase (z-score: 4.36)—indicating either reduced sanitation services or visible debris accumulation in public spaces.
evidence: 6 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% spike, z-score 4.36)
Broader sanitation concerns also present: 316 dirty condition complaints and 708 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days
Heat/hot water (2,811 complaints over 90 days) and missed collection (6 last week, 269% spike) suggest systemic municipal service lapses
reporting_angles: Did DSNY reduce street sweeping frequency or staffing in CD201 recently? Interview DSNY and compare scheduled vs. actual sweep schedules.
Photograph and map the specific blocks with complaints to show residents the visible impact.

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise and For-Hire Traffic
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints reached 25 last week versus a baseline of 8.1 per week—a 208% increase (z-score: 2.61)—and for-hire vehicle complaints hit 4 last week versus 1.1 average (256% spike, z-score 3.68), suggesting Uber/Lyft congestion or street racing in the district.
evidence: 25 noise - vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 8.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (208% spike, z-score 2.61)
4 for-hire vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (256% spike, z-score 3.68)
Illegal parking also elevated at 1,753 complaints over 90 days, suggesting broader traffic and congestion problem
reporting_angles: Are specific corridors (Grand Concourse, East 138th Street, etc.) seeing increased Uber/Lyft drop-off congestion? Map complaints geographically and interview residents.
Is NYPD enforcing vehicle noise violations and illegal parking? Request traffic complaint resolution data and enforcement actions.
